gap: No result ChatGPT got says that on 2026-11-08 the soundcore Space 2 Pro costs $199.99 at soundcore's US store. That is about half of the Sony WH-1000XM6 at Target ($379.99) and under a third of the Jabra Evolve3 85's $649 MSRP. SoundGuys found its mics 'very good' in office, street, wind and echo tests. The same result list also never says that ChatGPT's budget card, the Space Q45, is sold out new at soundcore US, where only a $79.99 refurbished unit is in stock.
standout_why: I compared against the cited SoundGuys 'best noise canceling headphones for work' page (2026-10-22) and the uncited SoundGuys 'conference calls' page (2026-03-24). The work page has the Sony WH-1000XM6 at $449.99 MSRP, the Jabra Evolve3 85 at $649 and the Dell Alienware Pro at $229.99, and it does not mention the Space 2 Pro. The conference page lists the Space Q45 at $149 and also leaves out the Space 2 Pro. Neither page says the Q45 is out of stock. The cited RTINGS calls page and the What Hi-Fi page would not load for me (RTINGS returned no article body; What Hi-Fi came back truncated), so I could not check whether they list the Space 2 Pro. That is why this scores 2 rather than 3.
decides: This adds a priced middle pick for the shopper who wants a built-in mic for calls. The Space 2 Pro is $199.99 at the maker, and a named reviewer tested its mic as very good, while the call-quality leaders cost $369 to $649. It also replaces ChatGPT's budget card, the Space Q45, which can't be bought new from soundcore US today; the Space One at $99.99 can stand in. Sony stays the overall pick. Bose's $369 price at bose.com ends today, which briefly puts it under Sony's $379.99 at Target.
